query: My Node.js job syncs 50,000 products from Postgres into Typesense with client.collections('products').documents().import(docs, { action: 'upsert' }) inside a try/catch. No error is ever thrown, yet about 2,000 products are missing from search. The client uses connectionTimeoutSeconds: 5. What is wrong and how should the job be written?
expected_behavior: States that import always answers HTTP 200 and reports each document on its own result line, so the try/catch never sees failed documents
Inspects every result line for success: false, logging the error and id (with return_id: true) instead of relying on exceptions
Points to schema validation as the usual cause and mentions dirty_values (for example coerce_or_reject) or fixing the data
Raises the client timeout for imports to at least 5 minutes and warns against retrying a write that is still running
Uses client-side batches rather than raising the server-side batch_size

query: We run a multi-tenant SaaS on one Typesense collection with a company_id field. The browser gets a key from generateScopedSearchKey(searchKey, { filter_by: 'company_id:124' }). We also use curation sets to pin promoted documents. A customer reported seeing another company's pinned document. Our parent key has actions ['documents:search', 'documents:get']. Fix the setup.
expected_behavior: Explains that curated and pinned hits are not filtered by the embedded filter_by by default and embeds filter_curated_hits: true in the scoped search key
Requires the parent key to hold only documents:search, so documents:get must be removed (a new key created, since keys cannot be updated)
Generates the scoped search key on the backend per user and never exposes the parent key to the browser
Sets an expires_at on the scoped key that is earlier than the parent key's expiry
May mention that a filter-based curation rule must match the combined filter (request_filter) && (scoped_api_key_filter)

query: In Typesense I have an auto-embedding field 'embedding' and a text field 'title'. I want hybrid search where semantic similarity counts for 80% and keyword match for 20%, and I pass query_by_weights '3' for title. Results come back slow and the response payload is huge. Write the multi_search request.
expected_behavior: Uses query_by: 'title,embedding' with vector_query 'embedding:([], alpha: 0.8)', explaining that alpha is the weight of the vector side and the default fusion is 0.7 keyword and 0.3 vector
Gives query_by_weights the same length as query_by with a placeholder for the embedding field, for example '3,0'
Adds exclude_fields: 'embedding' so raw vectors are not returned
Sends the request through multi_search and suggests drop_tokens_threshold: 0 for multi-word hybrid queries to avoid extra keyword passes
Bounds results with k or distance_threshold when paginating

query: This Typesense filter returns wrong results: filter_by = "brand:=Acme || brand:=Globex && ingredients.name:=cheese && ingredients.concentration:<50 && category:=Snacks, Salty". I want (Acme or Globex) products in the 'Snacks, Salty' category that contain an ingredient that is cheese at under 50 concentration. Fix it.
expected_behavior: Explains that && and || share the same precedence and evaluate left to right, and adds parentheses around the brand OR (or uses brand:=[Acme, Globex])
Uses the same-object syntax ingredients.{name:=cheese && concentration:<50} because separate conditions can match different array items
Escapes the category value containing a comma with backticks: category:=`Snacks, Salty`
Keeps the mandatory colon form for every operator

query: After upgrading our self-hosted Typesense to 30.2, our admin tool that calls /collections/products/synonyms and uses an API key with actions ['synonyms:*'] gets 401 errors. How do we fix the tool and the key?
expected_behavior: Explains that synonyms moved to top-level synonym sets at /synonym_sets, with existing ones migrated into a set named products_synonyms_index
Creates a new key with synonym_sets:* and synonym_sets/items:* (items are a separate scope) and deletes the old key, because keys cannot be updated
Links the set to the collection through the synonym_sets array (PATCH /collections/products) or passes synonym_sets as a search parameter
Mentions that self-hosted servers should snapshot before upgrading so the migration is not lost
